{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZbRZ5A", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhDCm_I", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 43, "title": "Resolve and implement OAM port addressing outside forced blank and VBlank", "body": "## Problem

At baseline `f1e3a668339cf52eead622d00ec915ea7952b721`, OAMDATA ($2104) writes and RDOAM ($2138) reads always access software-addressed OAM. Neither path checks display state. Both advance the same byte address unconditionally. This leaves OAM access during rendering indistinguishable from ordinary blanked access.

The latest assessment identifies this as the next bounded investigation. Issue #41 corrected VRAM access and expressly left OAM restrictions/corruption unresolved; its VRAM rules must not become an unsupported OAM contract. No open Issue or completed improvement in the supplied history covers this behavior.

## Expected outcome

Implement a source-backed distinction between software-addressed OAM access during permitted blanking and OAM address ownership during rendering, including the address/latch effects needed to recover correctly into permitted access. CPU, DMA and HDMA must use the same PPU port semantics.

A concrete prerequisite is resolving the OAM-specific specification. This evaluator inspected only the repository and supplied context. The raw reference copies mentioned in the validation records are absent from this checkout; no external specifications were fetched. Consequently, restricted-period destination addresses, returned bytes, latch effects and address restoration are **unresolved**, not verified requirements. Do not implement a guessed VRAM-style gate and describe it as hardware accuracy.

### Specification contract

Use these hardware research references, already cited by the repository:

- [Anomie's Register Doc, revision 1157](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt): flag legend, INIDISP, OAMADDL/OAMADDH, OAMDATA and OAMDATAREAD.
- [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm): OAM access registers, INIDISP, and PPU memory-access/timing sections.

The repository's existing accessible-period model is precise: $2102/$2103 select a nine-bit word address; port accesses advance a ten-bit byte address; addresses with bit 9 set mirror into the 32-byte high table; low-table writes latch the even byte and commit a pair on the odd byte; high-table writes commit directly. These are existing implementation/test expectations, with Fullsnes attribution in the [Issue #5 validation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-5-validation.md#hardware-semantics-and-licensed-test-results). Confirm their exact applicability and latch side effects against the register descriptions before extending them across display transitions.

Before changing production behavior, record an operation/state table covering:

| Operation | States requiring an explicit rule |
| --- | --- |
| $2102/$2103 writes | Forced blank, VBlank, active display, HBlank, scanline 0 |
| $2104 even/odd low-table writes | Same states; latch capture, pair commitment and address advancement separately |
| $2104 high-table writes | Same states; mirroring and shared-latch effects separately |
| $2138 reads | Same states; effective address, returned-byte support and advancement separately |
| Entry/exit from blanking | Programmed versus internal address, write phase/latch preservation, and any documented restoration event |

For each rule, cite the exact reference section, version and qualification. Distinguish established behavior, disagreement and unknown electrical values. In particular, unavailable software-addressed access does **not** by itself establish discarded writes, CPU/PPU open-bus returns, retained bytes, frozen addresses, or HBlank permission. Correct earlier documentation or tests if the references contradict their contract.

Implement the resolved behavior. Where an exact rendering-owned address or electrical byte requires the absent fetch pipeline, document a narrowly bounded deterministic approximation and test it as emulator policy. Do not label those values hardware-verified.

## Context and reproduction

Relevant inspected evidence:

- [PPU implementation](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/src/ppu.rs): `write`, lines 124–147, reconstructs OAM address and performs unconditional OAM writes; `read`, lines 225–233, performs unconditional software-addressed reads and increments. `objects` also uses the live address for priority rotation, so address changes need a composition regression.
- The same file's `oam_pairs_high_table_mirror_and_cgram_open_bit_are_separate_latches` test initializes `Ppu::default()` with forced blank enabled. It covers a low-table pair and one high-table mirror, without restricted-period or transition coverage.
- [Machine routing and timing](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs): CPU accesses commit after their timed access; DMA/HDMA share `transfer`, sampling the source after four clocks and committing the destination four clocks later. `tick` currently uses fixed lines and VBlank beginning at line 225.
- [Issue #41 evidence and limitations](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/docs/issue-41-validation.md) distinguishes source facts from approximation policy and leaves OAM behavior outstanding.
- [Existing natural-scheduler VRAM tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/src/machine/ppu_vram_tests.rs) and [CPU guests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/crates/snes-core/tests/ppu_vram_access.rs) provide patterns for register initialization, synchronization and bounded observation.

A baseline reproduction should initialize distinct OAM sentinels through executed port writes under forced blank, select a distinguishable address, release blanking, synchronize to stable active display, and access $2104/$2138. Current code continues ordinary software-addressed access. Derive the corrected assertions from the resolved OAM contract rather than recording current emulator output.

### Focused scope and non-goals

Scope is OAM port address ownership, associated byte-phase/latch progression, and the documented blanking transitions necessary for recovery. Include shared CPU/DMA/HDMA routing and preservation of ordinary sprite composition.

Do not add a complete object-fetch pipeline, general raster renderer, overflow evaluation, rectangular/object-interlace support, CGRAM changes, display modes, PAL, DMA alignment redesign, UI work or game-specific exceptions. Exact active-display corruption and physical access strobes remain explicitly unresolved wherever the selected references and current architecture cannot establish them.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Resolve and record the operation/state table above before implementation. Cite source versions and exact supporting sections, identify conflicts, and explain any approximation. The evidence prerequisite does not permit closing this implementation Issue with documentation alone.
- [ ] Change production OAM behavior for the established missing distinction. Include at least one original regression that fails on this baseline and passes with the implementation. Keep source-supported assertions separate from approximation-policy assertions.
- [ ] Add independent PPU vectors for low-table pairs, high-table mirrors, even/odd accesses, address wrap, interleaved reads/writes, both address registers, and transitions into/out of permitted access. Assert affected memory, address and latch state; do not use production helpers as the expected-value oracle.
- [ ] Add natural-scheduler bus tests for stable active display, HBlank, forced blank, VBlank and scanline 0. Exercise relevant VBlank/frame-wrap boundaries using ordinary timed accesses. Boundary assertions must identify retained scheduler conventions rather than claim physical-strobe accuracy.
- [ ] Exercise forward/reverse DMA and direct/indirect HDMA through the affected OAM ports, with permitted-access controls. Assert port effects plus transfer counts, addresses, table progression and termination. Do not require unspecified electrical-byte constants as hardware assertions.
- [ ] Add an original MIT CPU guest integration target named `ppu_oam_access`. The guest must initialize OAM, synchronize, perform accesses, recover to permitted access, and publish numeric results and a completion marker. Host code supplies the ROM and observes results; it must not patch CPU, raster, PPU or result state. Enforce instruction/frame deadlines and document provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Preserve existing sprite composition, priority-rotation controls, VRAM/counter/DMA/HDMA regressions and all cleared-game assertions. Run the following pre-merge gates using the README toolchain setup:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo test --locked -p snes-core --test ppu_oam_access
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
npm --prefix web test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds'
```

Use the documented `SNES_TEST_PORT` override if necessary. Preserve both cleared games' five-minute replays, Castle's full route, Memory's gameplay/audio checks and existing browser assertions. Preserve source pins, fixture/game hashes, notices and licensing decisions. Acquire no commercial ROM or firmware.

- [ ] Record actual commands, results, baseline counterexamples and remaining uncertainty. Update README accuracy limits without claiming full OAM accuracy, full hardware accuracy or commercial compatibility. This read-only evaluation ran no tests.
- [ ] Preserve all 24 inventory categories and their supplied outstanding scope. The 20 partial categories remain `cpu`, `bus`, `scheduler`, `dma`, `hdma`, `controllers`, `ppu-bg`, `ppu-offset`, `ppu-mode7`, `ppu-objects`, `ppu-color`, `ppu-ports`, `ppu-display`, `spc`, `ipl`, `dsp-noise`, `dsp-pitch`, `dsp-envelope`, `dsp-echo`, `dsp-timing`; `dsp-voices` remains `implemented_unverified`; `ppu-hires`, `ppu-raster`, `pal` remain unimplemented. Specifically retain unresolved CGRAM access/corruption, VRAM invalid-fetch bits, physical blanking/access boundaries, external latch inputs, long-dot/field conversion and warm-reset retention. This Issue completes no whole category or historical Issue #3 requirement.

## Optional validation

None required. Existing legally sourced hardware measurements may supplement the specification record, but physical-device access and subjective approval are not completion conditions.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
